name: Blaster
abilities: Your Actions may apply to one extra target within range.
When you add Blaster Form to a Style, increase that Style's maximum range by 1.

actions.name: Amplify
actions.text: Your next Action this turn has its maximum range increased by 3, and may apply to one additional target.

actions.name: Shockwave
actions.text:
Unblockable by Armor and Shields. Deal 1 damage to each enemy within range.
6+: Deal 2 damage to one enemy within range.

skill.name: Basically Magic
skill.text: You have an ability that's beyond normal, like lycanthropy, telekinesis, fire magic, ghost powers, or something else. When you take this skill, write down what kind of power you have.

description: Blaster Form is the multi-targetting master, giving an extra target to every Action you perform. Blaster makes every active type of Style better. Support Styles support more allies, aggro Styles damage more enemies, technical Styles ruin more folks' days, and so on. The Blaster Ability allows you to apply your Actions to an additional target for free, every time you use an Action. This extra target is optional, and cannot target anything the Action is already targeting. You can't 'double up.' If you cannot use the extra target, you do not get to use it. The extra target granted by the Blaster Ability must be within your range, in addition to any targeting limitations provided by the Action itself. So if the Action targets "one enemy within sight", your extra target must be within sight AND within range. If the Action targets "one adjacent enemy," but your Stance has a minimum range of 2, you cannot apply the Blaster Ability's extra target, because no enemy is both within range and adjacent to you. Amplify does not have this limitation. Its extra target may be any legal target, from within the Action's normal targetting options. Actions that target only yourself, like Unbreakable Style's Eyes Open, gain no benefit from Amplify or the Blaster Ability. Valid extra targets include any enemy, ally, or obstacle the Action could have targeted normally, as long as that target is also within your range. If an Action places obstacles, you may use one extra target to place one more of those obstacles. If an Action targets multiple kinds of targets, you decide which one(s) you want to apply your extra target(s) to. You choose what you want your extra target(s) to be as you take the Action. For example, Zombie Style's Raise The Dead targets one enemy, then places two Copy obstacles adjacent to that enemy. You may use your extra target to either target a second enemy (letting you place two Copies adjacent to each enemy), or you could use your extra target to place a third Copy adjacent to the initial enemy. Frantic Heroes increase the maximum range of the Style they attach to Blaster Form when they make their Stance. Tiered Actions get stronger if you spend a bigger number to use them. These Actions have multiple costs listed, known as Gates. These Actions also list these Gates in their text. When you are performing an Action and reach a Gate you did not pay for, the Action ends. If you spend a 3, 4, or 5 to perform Shockwave, you stop performing the Action when you reach the 6+ Gate. If you spend a 6 or any larger number on a Shockwave, you will perform the entire Action.

name: Control
abilities: After you spend Control Tokens, you may Push 1 or Pull 1 to the enemy whose Action you Controlled.
When you add Control Form to a Style, choose one:
• Increase that Style's maximum range by 3.
• Set that Style's minimum range to 0.

actions.name: Suppression
actions.text:
You gain 1 Control token and may Move 1.
6+: You gain 1 Control token and may Move 1.
9+: You gain 1 Control token and may Move 1.

skill.name: Professional
skill.text: You always look stylish, cool, and in control. People listen when you make demands of them, and you have some lackeys or followers who will do what you say.

description: Control Form is the counterspell, the negate, the tech cancel of Panic at the Dojo. Control Tokens are a powerful but limited resource that can copy, dodge, or parry anything a foe throws your way. You just need to be within range, and Control's range boost helps with that. Control Token: A Unique token primarily granted by Control Form. After an enemy within your range declares and pays for an Action, but before they perform it, you have an opportunity to spend Control Tokens. You may spend 1 Control Token to Copy that Action, 2 Control Tokens to Dodge that Action, or 3 Control Tokens to Parry that Action. Control Tokens may only be used once per turn. Copy: After the Action resolves, you may perform the same Action immediately, as a Reactive Action. For X Values and Gates, use a value of 4. You cannot Copy an Action that is only usable once per turn. Dodge: You or an ally within your range become immune to the Action. That Action will deal no damage, give no tokens, cause no forced movement, and apply no other effects to the one who Dodged it. Parry: The Action is negated and immediately ends. Then, you deal 2 damage to the one who used the Parried Action, and may Move up to 2. Super Moves are not Actions, and cannot be Controlled. Frantic Heroes decide whether to increase the maximum range or decrease the minimum range of the Style they attach to Control Form, when they make their Stance. They are not "locked in" to this decision, and may make a different decision when making the same Stance later, even if Control Form is being attached to the same Style. Range: 0 is the space you are in. Having Range: 0 allows you to target enemies standing in the same space as you are. This mostly applies against Giants, Vehicles, or Weightless Style, which all grant the ability to share spaces with enemies or allies. Unique Tokens are tokens only used in a few places, by specific Archetypes, Styles or Forms. These Tokens are described wherever they are generated. Unique Tokens share the color of the source that generates them - purple for Archetypes, blue for Forms, or red for Styles. Unique Tokens include Control Tokens, Chaos Tokens, Mentor Tokens, Luck Tokens, Poltergeist Tokens, Training Tokens, and others. When someone takes an Action while it is not their turn, it is known as a Reactive Action. Reactive Actions can only be performed after the active player completes an Action, and can never interrupt an Action while it is being resolved. All enemies and all players get the chance to take a Reactive Action during this window, before the active player may continue to take their turn as normal. Reactive Actions include: Token Actions; Free Actions; Dice Actions when something grants you a number outside of your turn (Reversal Form, the Sing Along Action, etc); using a Chaos Token to take an immediate Action; an Action Stolen by a Control Token; or anything an Ability allows you to do during someone else's turn. Allies get the chance to use Reactive Actions before enemies do. Once all Reactive Actions are resolved, the active character regains priority, and may take another Action. When the active character has no more Actions to resolve, all other characters may each make one last Reactive Action, before ending the Action Phase and starting the Late Movement Phase.

name: Dance
abilities: After you take damage, pay HP, or are healed, you gain 1 Speed token.
When you Bleed, gain 3 Speed tokens.

After each Dice Action you perform, if it applied Forced Movement to an enemy, they must discard 1 Basic token, if they have any. If it applied Forced Movement to an ally, they heal 1. If it moved, swapped, or teleported you, you heal 1.

actions.name: Dance Together
actions.text:
Choose someone within range. Pull them 1, then you Move 1, then you Pull them 1 more.
Usable once per turn.

actions.name: Tango
actions.text:
Swap spaces with an adjacent enemy, then Push them 1.
6+: Pull them 2, then deal 2 damage to them.
10+: Push them 4, then deal 3 damage to them.

actions.name: Dance Apart
actions.text:
Push 3 to someone within range, then Move 1.
7+: Move 2 more, then heal.

skill.name: Put On A Show
skill.text: You can draw as much attention as you want, whenever you want it, away from anything else, for any reason.

description: Dance Form excels in repositioning at any moment. You slide across the battlefield as you wish, dragging along enemy and ally alike as you go. A Dancer can never be pinned down, and must always be pursued. The first Dance Ability will gain 1 Speed token for each triggered instance. If an Action deals 1 damage to you, then 2 damage to you, you will gain 2 Speed tokens from that Action. The key to a powerful Dancer is in using their Token Actions at just the right moment. How you use your Reactive Actions separates the lesser Dancers from the Olympic contenders. Token Actions are Actions that cost something other than a number to perform. Like the name implies, they usually require you to spend some tokens, but not always - they may have you spend your Shield, or pay using your HP. As the only kind of Action that doesn't require numbers in your Action Pool, you can always use Token Actions during other's turns, as Reactive Actions, if you can afford them. Speed Tokens: Speed tokens are basic tokens that grant Free Movement. Speed Tokens are primarily used by Dance Form and Shadow Form, but they are common in many Archetypes and Styles. While you hold any speed tokens, you may move one space in any direction at any time before each Action you perform. You can use Free Movement during enemy turns, but only during the Movement Phases, or to Save Yourself. After you use Free Movement, you must discard Speed Tokens. You discard your tokens after moving, so even if you only have 1 Speed token, you can still use it to move diagonally and/or onto Rubble. If you moved laterally (up, down, left, or right), discard 1 Speed token. If you moved diagonally, discard 2 Speed tokens. If you moved onto Rubble, you gain 1 Fatigue token. You cannot use Free Movement if you have no Speed tokens. After any Forced Movement that pushes or pulls you onto Rubble, a Trap, a Pit, or Outside, you can spend 1 Speed token to move 1 Space immediately. If you do, you do not suffer the effects of that space. You do not gain Fatigue from Rubble, or take damage from a Trap or a Pit, or get removed from play by going Outside the Grid. At the end of each turn, everyone discards 3 Speed tokens.

name: Iron
abilities: You have Armor.
When your Armor triggers, you gain 1 Iron token.
When you gain Speed tokens, replace half of them (rounded down) with Iron tokens.
You may spend 1 Iron token to take 1 less damage from any source (even Reduced Hits).

actions.name: Secure
actions.text: Choose two: Gain 2 Iron tokens; -or- an ally within range other than yourself gains 2 Iron tokens; -or- give Shield 2 to an ally within range.

actions.name: Contain
actions.text: Target an enemy within range, then Choose two: Challenge them; -or- Give them 2 Fatigue tokens; -or- place a Trap into their space.

actions.name: Protect
actions.text: Choose four from the Secure and Contain lists. Options from the Contain list must target an enemy within range.

skill.name: Immovable
skill.text: When you plant your feet and stand your ground, nothing can get past you or hurt you, not even vehicles or gunfire.

description: Iron Form is unbreakable, a dominant and incredibly tough Form that can take hit after hit after hit and remain standing after it all. The final Iron Ability can reduce 1 damage from any source of damage. It can reduce an already Reduced Hit. It can reduce damage from Pits or from Traps, or from Burning Tokens. It can even reduce damage from an Unblockable Action that normally prevents Iron tokens! For ordering purposes, Protect goes through the Secure list before going through the Contain list. Once you start resolving the Contain effects, target an enemy within range for them to apply to. If you have Armor from multiple sources, then each time any of your Armor triggers, the Iron Ability will give you 1 Iron token. It does not have to be specifically Iron Form's Armor, any Armor will do. Traps: When you move into a space with a Trap, it deals 1 damage to everyone in that space. At the end of every single turn, everyone standing on a Trap takes 1 damage. Each Trap can only deal damage once per turn. Armor is a once per turn, automatic block. The first time each turn that you take damage, if you have Armor, reduce that damage by 3. This can apply to any type of damage, including Fall damage, burning token damage, Super Move damage, or damage dealt by a Trap. HP costs (such as paying for Lash Out, Heart Strike, or Forbidden Style) are not damage, and so they are not reduced by Armor. Armor stacks, as well. If you have Armor from two sources, such as being in Lucky Iron Stance, then your Armor can trigger twice per turn. However, additional Armor triggers are weaker - the second time Armor triggers in the same turn, it only blocks 2 damage. The third time and beyond, Armor only blocks 1 damage. If you take damage that ignores Armor, your Armor does not trigger. Some Abilities grant temporary Armor, which is used after all other Armor and only triggers once. Once your temporary Armor has triggered, it is lost. Temporary Armor is a binary - you either have it or you do not. You cannot have multiple instances of temporary Armor. Iron Tokens are basic tokens that grant damage reduction on demand. Iron tokens are primarily used by Iron Form and Tricksters, but they are common across many Archetypes and Styles. When you take damage from an Action or Ability, you may spend 1 Iron token to Reduce it. A Reduced Hit deals 1 less damage. When you suffer Forced Movement (a Push or a Pull), you may spend 1 Iron token to Resist it. A Resisted Force moves you 2 less spaces, to a minimum of zero spaces moved. Iron Tokens cannot Reduce damage from other sources, like Traps, Burning Tokens, Pits, or Super Moves.

name: One-Two
abilities: Before each Action you perform, you may Move 1.
After your first Action on your turn, Move 1, then deal 2 damage to an enemy within range.
At the end of each turn where you performed any Actions, you may deal 1 damage to an enemy within range, then Move 2.

actions.name: Slide In
actions.text:
Teleport 2.
4+: Teleport 2 more, then you may deal 1 damage to an enemy within range.

actions.name: Left, Right!
actions.text: Deal 1 damage to an enemy within range, then deal 2 damage to a different enemy within range.

skill.name: Think Fast
skill.text: You can come up with plans and act on them in an instant. You never lose in games of skill, and you can fast talk anyone into seeing things your way.

description: One-Two is a highly aggressive skirmisher Form, focused on only two things: Dealing damage, and getting closer so you can deal damage. One-Two Form is a rushdown player's dream. One-Two's Abilities are not Actions, so when you use an Ability that triggers off of dealing damage with an Action, One-Two's Abilities do not trigger that Ability again. The extra hits from One-Two's Abilities will remove a Weakness token you hold.This makes One-Two Form excellent for both removing your own Weakness tokens, as well as triggering enemy Armor, to let you get hits in past their defenses. Movement comes in 6 types: Free Movement, Action Movement, Teleportation, Swapping Spaces, Forced Movement, or Saving Yourself. Movement can only be used to enter empty spaces, regardless of the movement type. You cannot enter full spaces. A full space is any space with a Wall, a Copy, or another Unit already occupying it. Free Movement: Movement granted by spending Speed tokens. Each space costs 1 Speed token. On a square grid, diagonal movements cost 2 Speed tokens. Leaving a Pit costs +1 Speed token. On your turn, you may use Free Movement before each Action you take. On others' turns, you may only use Free Movement during the Early Movement Phase and the Late Movement Phase. Action Movement: Any movement granted by an Action or Ability. Move the listed number of spaces, stopping if you enter Rubble or a Pit. Teleportation: Movement that ignores intervening spaces. You directly enter the target space from your current space. You can teleport to any space within the max, and do not have to go the full distance. Swapping Spaces: Movement that switches your position with that of an obstacle, enemy, or ally. You teleport into the target's space and they teleport into yours, simultaneously. Forced Movement: A Push or Pull effect, almost always applied to you by someone else. Each space of a Push must be farther away from the Pusher than the previous space. Each space of a Pull must be closer to the Puller than the previous space. Saving Yourself: After someone uses Forced Movement on you, after the last space, you may spend 1 Speed token to move into an adjacent space of your choice and ignore any terrain effects from the space you dodged. Rubble will not give you Fatigue, Traps and Pits will not deal damage to you, and the Outside will not remove you from play.

name: Power
abilities: When you gain Speed tokens, replace half of them (rounded down) with Power tokens.
You can Enhance a Hit two additional times.

actions.name: Yell
actions.text: You gain Power tokens equal to half of X (rounded up), then you gain a Shield with a value equal to half of X (rounded down).

actions.name: Crush
actions.text:
Unblockable by Abilities and Tokens. Deal 3 damage to an enemy within range.
9+: Deal 5 damage instead, and Crush is Unblockable.

skill.name: Unstoppable
skill.text: You can smash through any door, wall, or vehicle.

description: Power Form has a very simple, very effective plan: yell really loud, then hit them really hard. What else do you need? When you gain an odd number of Speed tokens, the Power Ability keeps the odd token out as a Speed token. So if you should gain 5 Speed tokens, you instead gain 2 Power tokens and 3 Speed tokens. Normally, you can use 1 Power token to Enhance a Hit. The Power Ability allows you to use up to 3 Power tokens per hit, allowing you to turn even a weak 1 damage hit into a devastating 4 damage blow. Each Power token spent will add "Push 1", however, so they will be sent flying away! A full powered Crush is nearly unstoppable. Enemy tokens and Abilities cannot be used in response. On a 9+, they can't even use Armor! They just get Crushed. Power Tokens: Power tokens are basic tokens that give your attacks more impact. Power tokens are primarily used by Power Form, but they are common across many Archetypes and Styles. When you hit an enemy, you may spend up to 2 Power tokens. For each Power token spent, that hit deals 1 more damage and applies 1 more space of forced movement. Power tokens do not increase damage when Enhancing a hit with no damage, and they do not increase forced movement when Enhancing a hit with no forced movement. A "hit" is any individual attempt to deal damage or apply forced movement, and you spend Power tokens on each hit individually. You can spend a maximum of 2 Power tokens per hit. If you spend any Power tokens on a hit, you have Enhanced the hit. Abilities that trigger when you Enhance a hit only trigger when Power tokens are used to increase your damage or forced movement, not when spent on other things (like Token Actions). Damage Calculation: When someone deals damage to someone else, go through these steps to calculate the damage dealt. The one dealing damage is the Attacker, and the one taking it is the Target. 1. Determine base damage. 2. If the attacker has Weakness tokens, discard one and reduce the damage by 2. 3. Weird effects go here. 4. The attacker may spend 1 Power token to increase the damage dealt by 1 and add "Push 1". 5. The target may now spend 1 Iron token to reduce the damage by 1, and may spend 1 Iron token to reduce any Forced Movement by 2. 6. The target decides what to block with their Shield: either damage or a type of Status Token. 7. If the damage number is still 1 or higher, and the target hasn't used their Armor yet this turn, reduce the damage by 3. 8. If the final number is positive, reduce the target's health by that much, then the Attacker applies all on-hit and on-damage effects to the target. 9. If the target has any Abilities that trigger from taking damage or being hit, those apply now. If the final damage was zero, do not trigger on-damage effects. On-hit effects are still applied.

name: Reversal
abilities: You have Armor.
Unblockable by Control Tokens and Iron Tokens.
The first time your Armor triggers each turn, you may Teleport 2. Then, if your Action Pool is empty, add a 3 to your Action Pool.

actions.name: Palm Strike
actions.text: Push 3 and deal 1 damage to an adjacent enemy.

actions.name: Deep Breathing
actions.text:
Move up to 2. This movement ignores obstacles. At the start of the next turn, add X to your Action Pool.
Usable once per turn. Unblockable.

actions.name: Rupture
actions.text:
An enemy within range gains X Burning Tokens.
This can only target the active character.

skill.name: Perfect Timing
skill.text: You are always in the right place at the right time. You can perfectly catch or stop anything coming directly at you with a single, well-placed motion.

description: Reversal Form takes its turn slowly, throughout the entire Round. They act when needed, and at no other times. With the right Action at the right time, you can steal an entire turn away. Reversal's Ability triggers when your Armor triggers, no matter how you did it. If you step into a Trap, bam! Gain a 3 . Numbers gained during the End Phase of a turn will not be discarded during that turn, so standing on a Trap will give you a 3 for next turn when it triggers your Armor. Unblockable means "this defense can't be used." So, Iron Tokens cannot be used to reduce damage or resist force you deal, and Control Tokens cannot copy, dodge, or parry your Actions while in Reversal. Burning Tokens represent the status of delayed damage, whether you are on fire, bleeding out, or poisoned. Burning Tokens are primarily used by Reversal Form and the Flametongue. At the end of your turn, if you have any Burning tokens, you take damage equal to the number of Burning tokens you hold. Then, you discard half of your Burning tokens, rounded up. For example, say you have 5 Burning tokens. When you end your turn, you will take 5 damage, then discard 3 of your Burning tokens, leaving you with 2 Burning tokens left. Burning token damage cannot be reduced by Iron tokens. Burning tokens eat through Shield HP before regular HP. Action Resolution: When you perform an Action, follow these steps: 1. Declare your Action. Pay any Costs required, and set the value of X (if applicable). Determine which Gates you will go through, and if it is not all of them, determine where your Action will stop. 2. If an enemy whose range you are within has Control Tokens, they get the option to Copy, Dodge, or Parry. 3. Go through the Action in order, as it is described. Declare targets as they come up in the Action. Make any Choices as they come up. If you reach a Gate you did not pay for, the Action ends. 4. If the target has a Shield, they decide what to block with it now, after seeing all that you will do to them. The Shield then eats the chosen damage or Status Tokens, one for one. 5. Once the Action has been resolved, any Abilities that trigger after Actions are now applied and resolved. The Abilities of the user resolve first, then the Abilities of any targets resolve next. Then, the Action is over.

name: Shadow
abilities: At the start and end of your turn, you gain 2 Speed tokens.
At the start of each Movement Phase, you may Move 1.
You do not discard any Speed tokens during the End Phase.

actions.name: Stunt
actions.text:
Place one Fog, Copy, Pit, or Trap obstacle into an adjacent space, then teleport 2.
During enemy turns: usable once per turn.

skill.name: Shadow Walker
skill.text: If you don't want to draw attention to yourself, no one will ever notice you sneaking around, even in plain sight.

description: Shadow Form skulks in the shadows, always moving and never stopping. While Dance Form repositions everyone, Shadow runs away and harries any pursuers instead, leaving obstacles as they go. Free Movement is granted by spending Speed tokens. When it is your turn, you can use Free Movement as much as you'd like before each Action you perform. Free Movement cannot be used mid-Action - once an Action begins resolving, you must completely resolve the Action before anything else can be done. When it is not your turn, you can only use Free Movement during the Movement Phases. You cannot use Free Movement between Actions when you are not the active character. Free Movement costs 1 Speed token per space. It costs 1 extra Speed token to leave a Pit. If you are playing on a square grid, it costs 1 extra Speed token to move diagonally. Even outside of Free Movement, you can use Speed Tokens to Save Yourself. After you suffer Forced Movement, you may spend 1 Speed token to immediately move one space. If you used this to move out of a Trap, Pit, or Rubble space that you would have landed in, you do not suffer damage or gain a Fatigue token - you dodged the danger. If you used this to escape the Outside, you are not removed from play. Copies: Copies are replicas of yourself. Copies can be targeted as either enemies or as obstacles, but cannot be targeted as allies. When the Original takes an Action, they may use that Action as though they were in the location of one of their Copies. You can move your Copies with Free Movement, by spending Speed tokens on them just as you would for yourself. Anything done to a Copy only happens to that Copy, and is not reflected onto the original. Copies have 1 HP. Copies cannot hold tokens or shields. If a Copy is reduced to zero HP, it is destroyed. Copies count as players, for the purposes of occupying spaces. Fog: Enemies inside or adjacent to Fog can only be targeted at Range 1. Allies in Fog can be targeted normally. For the purposes of Actions and Abilities, anyone benefiting from Fog is 'in Fog,' even if they are standing next to it. Pits: Pits are holes in the floor that you can fall in. While you are in a Pit, you take 1 less damage from all Actions or Abilities from Range 3+. All Forced Movement against you is reduced by 1, to a minimum of zero spaces moved. It is difficult to leave a Pit. When you enter a Pit from Forced Movement, that push or pull immediately ends, then you take 2 Fall damage. If a Pit is placed directly under you, you take 2 Fall damage. When leaving a Pit's space with Free Movement, it costs 1 additional Speed token to do so. If you are pushed or pulled from one pit into another pit, you do not take fall damage. If you move from one pit into another pit with Free Movement, it does not cost an additional Speed Token to do so. Traps: When you move into a space with a Trap, it deals 1 damage to everyone in that space. At the end of every single turn, everyone standing on a Trap takes 1 damage. Each Trap can only deal damage once per turn.

name: Song
abilities: At the start of your turn, choose your song: Iron, Power, or Speed. You gain 3 tokens of the chosen type, and each ally (other than yourself) gains 1 token of the chosen type.

actions.name: Sing Along
actions.text:
Target an ally you can see. Choose one: They discard one token; -or- they heal 2; -or- they gain 2 tokens from your song.
4+: They also choose one from the list.
6+: Add a 4 to their Action Pool.
Usable once per turn.

actions.name: Diss Track
actions.text:
Target an enemy you can see. Choose one to give them: 2 Burning tokens; -or- 2 Fatigue tokens; -or- 2 Weakness Tokens.
5+: They also choose one from the list.
6+: Pull 2 and Challenge them.

skill.name: Natural Charisma
skill.text: People naturally like you. Anyone who is not your enemy is your friend, even if you've just met them.

description: Song Form is the diva of support, improving not just yourself but your entire team. A good beat can pick up any team. Healing removes damage that has been taken. Healing can never take someone above the maximum hit points of their current health bar. If you heal someone at zero HP, they revive immediately, and may take turns and be attacked by enemies again. When healing does not list a number, it heals equal to the Heal Value, which is set by the Cinematic Weight of the fight. Choice Actions have you choose one or more options from a list. When performing a Choice Action, each choice is known as an option, and you must perform each option in the order listed. Any option you did not pick is ignored, and does not happen. Each choice must be different. When you use Sing Along, for example, you cannot pick "they heal" twice. If you chose "they heal," the second choice must be one of the other two options. Even though Sing Along and Diss Track force someone else to make the second choice, they still cannot choose the same option you chose. Challenge Tokens: Challenge tokens are a special Status Token. You can only hold 1 Challenge token at a time, and each Challenge has a name attached to it - "Redd's Challenge," for example. If you hold a Challenge token, the person named in that token is your Challenger. When an Action tells you to Challenge someone, it means "give them a Challenge token with your name on it." You cannot Challenge someone who is already holding your Challenge. If you are given a different Challenge token while you already hold one, you may choose whose Challenge you wish to keep. When you hold someone's Challenge, all of your damage-dealing Actions must include them as one of their targets. Actions without a damage-dealing component, and Actions that do not target enemies at all, are not affected by a Challenge. At the end of your turn, if you tried to deal damage to your Challenger this turn, discard their Challenge (even if that damage was reduced to zero). If your Challenger ever leaves play or falls to zero HP, everyone holding their Challenge discards it immediately. Fatigue Tokens: Fatigue Tokens slow you down. Fatigue Tokens eat Speed Tokens one- for-one. You can never hold both at once. Essentially, Fatigue and Speed tokens are like matter and anti-matter. They instantly disappear on contact. While you are holding any Fatigue tokens, whenever you try to Move or Teleport any number of spaces, discard 1 Fatigue token and reduce the number of spaces you would move by 2 (to a minimum of 1). If an Action teleports you to a specific space (like Suddenly...), you teleport to that space anyway, and still discard 1 Fatigue token. Pushes and Pulls affect you normally and do not make you discard Fatigue. At the end of your turn, if you did not move from the space you started your turn, you may discard up to 3 Fatigue tokens.

name: Thorns
abilities: At the start and end of your turn, you gain Shield 2.
After your Shield absorbs from an enemy Action, you deal 1 damage to them. If it broke your Shield, you deal 2 damage instead.

actions.name: Blossoms
actions.text:
You gain Shield 2 and choose one: Gain 1 Power token; -or- Move 1; -or- heal 1.
6+: Instead, gain Shield 4 and choose two.

actions.name: Brambles
actions.text:
This is a Token Action that costs your Shield. Deal 1 damage to up to X enemies within Range 1-X, then gain 1 Power token.
X is equal to the value of the destroyed Shield.
Usable twice per turn.

skill.name: Rose Heart
skill.text: You can redirect others' anger to more productive ends. Your soothing voice and gentle touch can calm rampaging beasts, unruly mobs, and anyone else acting out of hurt or anger.

description: Thorns Form is a sinister flower. Its defensive Shields are lined with thorns, damaging any foe that attacks you. But if they ignore you, your Brambles and Blossoms will grow out of control until nothing can stop you. Thorns Form puts its foes into a beautiful lose/lose scenario. One of Thorns Form's Action Dice is a preset number, and is not rolled. There is no "5" die, you just take a 5 into your Action Pool. Damage dealt to your Shield by an Ability will not trigger the Thorns Ability. The extra hit from One-Two is not damage from an Action, so you will not deal 1 damage back to them from that hit. If you are Challenged by an Angel, their Angel Ability will deal 1 damage to you. Even if that Challenge came from an Action, the actual damage was dealt by an Ability, so Thorns will not redirect it. X Actions include an X listed in their effect, and usually also cost X to perform. You can spend any number in your Action Pool to pay for an X Action, and the X listed in the effect is the same value as the number you used to pay for the Action. For example, if you spend a 4 point Shield to use Brambles, then the effect reads: "Deal 1 damage to up to 4 enemies within Range 1-4, then you gain 2 Power token." If the Action does not cost X, then the value of X will be defined in the Action's description. In Brambles' case, X is the value of the Shield used to pay for Brambles. Brambles will always give you 1 less Power token than the value of the Shield used to pay for it. Shields are used to deflect incoming harm, when you need them. They have a value that represents how much they can absorb. Shields can be used to block either Damage, a specific kind of Status Token, or Nothing, from any Action or Ability that includes you as a target. Your Shield will block everything of the chosen type. You can only hold one Shield at a time - if you gain a new Shield, you can either replace your old Shield or increase the value of your current Shield by 1, your choice. There is a Shield Cap of 8. You can never hold a Shield with a value of 9 or higher. When an Action or Ability targets you while you hold a Shield, you must decide how to use your Shield. It may be used to absorb Damage, Burning Tokens, Challenge Tokens, Fatigue Tokens, Weakness Tokens, or Nothing, at your discretion. It will absorb the chosen resource at a rate of 1 for 1. When your Shield absorbs its total value, it breaks, and the excess is applied to you as normal. Some Actions have inherent limitations, such as "Usable once per turn." These limitations cannot be circumvented by any means. Even if you have a way to increase the numbers listed in an Action, like Poltergeist Tokens, you cannot change an Action that says "Usable once per turn" to become usable twice per turn. It cannot be used a second time. Even if you can apply extra targets, such as from the Blaster Ability or Amplify, that cannot get past a limitation like "can only target the active character." You must only target the active character.

name: Vigilance
abilities: At the start of your turn, discard up to 2 Status tokens you hold; then, if you are Bleeding, you heal.
At the end of your turn, choose up to two enemies within range and give them each 1 Weakness token.

actions.name: Bow Down
actions.text:
Give 1 Weakness token to an enemy within range.
4+: Give 1 Weakness token to each enemy within range.

actions.name: Stand Strong
actions.text:
1+: Give 1 Power token to an ally within range.
3+: Heal that ally.
5+: Heal and give 1 Power token to a different ally within range.
Usable once per turn.

skill.name: Eyes Wide Open
skill.text: Your senses are unusually strong. You cannot be surprised by anything, and always have a chance to react first.

description: Vigilance Form is reliability incarnate. You always know exactly what numbers you will have, and you can guarantee being alive to take your turn thanks to its start of turn heal. And if you don't need the heal, you can get rid of pesky Status tokens that would stop your plans. Vigilance Form's Action Dice are preset numbers, and are not rolled. There is no "5" die, you just take a 5 into your Action Pool. Weakness Tokens: Weakness tokens represent the status of lost strength, whether you are drained of energy, blinded, or emotionally compromised. Whenever you deal damage, if you are holding any Weakness tokens, reduce that damage by 2, to a minimum of 0. Then, discard 1 Weakness token. Healing restores lost HP. You cannot heal above the HP value of your current health bar. When an effect heals you, it will either list a number (like Heal 3) and you heal that much damage, or it will just say "Heal." If a number is not listed, you heal equal to the Heal Value set by the fight's Cinematic Weight. Each health bar has an HP value determined by the Cinematic Weight of the fight. Your health is reduced when you take damage, and it is increased when you heal. When you have multiple health bars, you take damage to them one by one. When one health bar falls to zero, that health bar breaks, and you can no longer Heal past that point. The hit that broke your health bar does not carry into the next health bar, and the extra damage is lost. When a Health Bar becomes zero, it breaks and you become Dizzy until the end of this turn. If it was your last Health Bar, you are Taken Out. While you are Dizzy, you cannot take damage, you cannot perform Actions, and you exit your current Stance. You cannot enter a new Stance until you take a turn. You still become Dizzy even if you were Taken Out - if an ally heals you, you will get up, but you won't be in a Stance until the next time you take a turn. While you have no Stance, your Range is 1. Your Archetype Abilities and Build Abilities still apply, but anything your Stance gave you - Form Abilities, Style Abilities, and your Unique Actions - is not available to you. While you are Taken Out, you cannot take Actions and your Abilities are mostly deactivated, but not completely. Any part of an Ability that targets enemies or allies doesn't apply. Any part of an Ability that would provide passive rules or effects does not apply. What DOES apply are the parts that affect only yourself. Shadow Form still gives yourself Speed tokens, which you keep even while Taken Out. Vigilance Form still heals you, letting you pick yourself back up. If an Ability gets you back to a positive HP number, your Abilities return online and work as normal. If you heal as the first part of an Ability (such as with the Angel Archetype Abilities), you may continue to use the rest of that Ability, now that you are no longer Taken Out. Heroic Spirit: Even if a unit is taken out, they still take turns! When you've been Taken Out and you take a turn, your turn plays out mostly as normal, to begin with. You choose your Stance and roll your Action Dice for the turn. But, since you've been Taken Out, you don't use your Action Dice to take your own Actions - you choose another player, and give them the numbers you rolled. They take another turn, using your roll and their current Stance. This sharing of power is known as your Heroic Spirit.

name: Wild
abilities: After each Action you perform, if you are not Bleeding, you pay 1 HP.
At the start of your turn, you gain 2 Power tokens.
When you Bleed, add a 4 to your Action Pool.

actions.name: Pounce
actions.text:
Pull yourself 3 towards an enemy you can see.
Usable once per turn.

actions.name: Howl
actions.text:
Gain 1 Power token, then heal 4, then give 1 Weakness token to each enemy you can see.
Usable once per turn.

skill.name: Wind Runner
skill.text: You can leap to anywhere you can see, run along walls, run as fast as a car, and, if you have an explanation, fly.

description: Wild Form goes hard, harder than your body can handle. You rush in with overwhelming strength, able to pile on pain and use powerful Unique Actions with ease. But if that rush of power doesn't end the fight, you're in trouble, as you are left tired, burnt out, weak, and vulnerable. So if you go this hard, you best not miss. The Bleed Value is set by the Cinematic Weight of the fight. While your current HP is equal to the Bleed Value or less, you are Bleeding. You are still considered to be Bleeding while you are at zero HP. When you take damage that reduces your HP to the Bleed Value or less, you Bleed. You can only Bleed once per Round. If you heal above the Bleed Value and fall below it again during the same Round, you will not re-trigger your Build Ability. If a new Round starts and your HP is below the Bleed Value, "When you Bleed" Abilities will not trigger until you take damage during that Round. There are three categories of Action, determined by their cost: Dice Actions, Token Actions, and Free Actions. Dice Actions cost a number to use, and can only be used while you have numbers in your Action Pool. Token Actions cost anything else, and can only be used when you have their cost available to spend. Free Actions have no cost at all, and can be used whenever you are able to use an Action. You can use a Free Action as a Reactive Action, or as a regular Action when you are the active character. Any Action you perform without paying its Cost becomes a Free Action, as well. Free Actions do not count as Dice Actions or Token Actions - they are their own, separate Action type. They are usually only granted by Abilities or Actions, like the Gunkata Abilities, Demon's Chaos Tokens, Seize The Opening, and Teacher's Remember Your Training. There is a Token Cap of 10. You can never have more than 10 tokens of a single type. You can have 10 tokens of as many token types as you want, but as soon as you would gain an 11th token of any type, you stop gaining those tokens, and remain at 10. All tokens share this Cap: Basic tokens, Status tokens, and Unique tokens all. The only exception is the Challenge token. Each unit can only hold one Challenge at a time, so they effectively have a Token Cap of 1.
